 Warriors Host North Dakota State Looking For Third Straight Win
 Story Links
 HONOLULU – The University of Hawai'i football team returns to Ching Complex for its first home game in nearly a month when it hosts North Dakota State on Saturday at 6 p.m. The Rainbow Warriors will look to extend their winning streak to three games and keep their hopes of bowl eligibility alive when they take on the Bison for the first time ever. Saturday's game will also be UH's first home game since the passing of legendary  Hawai'i head coach June Jones. Throughout the game, Jones will be honored with messages and tributes while the team will wear "JJ" helmet stickers in his honor. 
 Promotions :
 Heineken is the title sponsor for Saturday's Military Night  contest. 
 Fans are asked to WEAR BLACK in honor of the late, legendary head coach of the Warrior football program, June Jones.
 Throughout the game remembrances and video tributes to Jones will be played, in addition to a pregame moment of silence.
 The first 3,000 fans will receive a  Timmy Chang  mini bobblehead featuring the record-setting QB.
 Active duty, DOD civilians, reservists, and retired members of the military have access to 50% off select tickets. A valid Military ID is required to pick up will call tickets. Click  here  to purchase tickets.
 Military marching bands will perform alongside the UH Marching Band.
 A military aircraft flyover will celebrate Veterans Day Weekend.
 The  Rooftop Pā'ina  is an elevated pregame experience for Rainbow Warrior football home games on the fifth floor of Zone 20 parking structure. The event is free although a parking pass to park in the structure is required. Click here for more info. 
 New VIP Experiences are available for fans, including Sideline Tables, the Makai Beach Club and a VIP Tailgate Area. Click here for more info.

 SERIES VS NORTH DAKOTA STATE Series Information : First Meeting 
 GAME STORYLINES 
 Hawai'i and North Dakota State will meet for the first time ever on Saturday.
 The Warriors have won their last two games after starting the season 1-6, meaning UH still has a chance to qualify for a bowl game by winning their final three contests.
 UH's last two wins have both come on the road, marking the first time since 2007 that the Warriors have won both legs of a back-to-back road stretch.
 The Warriors will be playing their first home game since the passing of legendary head coach June Jones. Jones is the program's all-time winningest coach and coached five members of the UH coaching staff, including Chang who became the NCAA's all-time leading passer under Jones' guidance.
 In nine years under Jones, UH finished in the top four nationally in passing each season running the Run N' Shoot offense that produced numerous record-setting QBs such Chang and Heisman Trophy finalist Colt Brennan.
 The Warriors will wear special "JJ" stickers on their helmets throughout the remainder of the season to honor their legendary former head coach.
 UH returns home for the first time in nearly a month coming off of wins at Northern Illinois (56-21) and at UTEP (17-14).
 QB Micah Alejado is third nationally with 25.3 completions per game and 202 total pass completions. He also leads the Mountain West in passing yards per game (276.6) and total offense (276.4).
 Alejado moved into sixth place on UH's all-time career passing yards chart during last week's win, now totaling 6,180 career passing yards while becoming the ninth Warrior signal-caller to eclipse the 6,000-yard mark. (see full list on Pg. 4)
 WR Titan Lacaden was named Mountain West Freshman of the Week after turning a career day with 11 receptions for 109 yards and a touchdown. His 11 catches are the most by a UH player this year, and second-most by an FBS freshman in 2026.
 UH is 6-2 in November home games under head coach Timmy Chang , including three straight wins in the final month of the season dating back to 2024. UH's only two November home losses under Chang have been by one possession each (2024 vs. UNLV, 29-27; 2022 vs. Utah State (41-34).
